utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier, April Carter, and Barney Thomas for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Chad Mair, Tina Drolec, Oonagh O'Connor, and Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, Mr. Kadijevic. Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kadijevic, I had an opportunity to go over the transcript of the proceedings yesterday and in reviewing them I came across something which I believe may well be a translation error, and I'd like to double-check something with you. Yesterday at page 13533, lines 7 through 14, with regard to the question of what your responsibilities were while you were in the position of assistant minister of defence, you stated: "The main task in that position was to co-ordinate within the sector for military economic activities in order to fulfill the duties and obligations of the Army of Yugoslavia when it comes to funding equipment and weaponry. In order to complete my task, I was superior to the Institute For Research And Development of the Army of Yugoslavia, and it dealt with research and development as well as the development of the special military industry, special-purpose military industry which was to produce the equipment and weaponry needed for the military." My question to you, sir, is with regard to the language that is contained herein, in order to complete your task when you say you were superior to the Institute For Research And Development, was that for the Army of Yugoslavia, the Ministry of Defence? Could you kindly explain because I believe that it would have been for the development of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the most important research and development institution and it was on the strength and it was subordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say what was the most important research and development institution, what I'm trying to get an understanding of here is with regard to what you told us yesterday -- I'm told now that there definitely was a translation error, by my colleague who speaks B/C/S, and I was told that he said -- his answer was that it was subordinate to the Federal Ministry of Defence. Once again I'm trying to get some understanding here as to whether that's the Army of Yugoslavia or the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest that when you are told that there was a translation error, rather than tell us what the error was, get the witness to repeat himself before you say what the error was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you repeat yourself, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Military Technical Institute, as the most important research and development institution, was part of the Federal Ministry of Defence and it was directly subordinated to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to your duties in terms of the issue of research and development, from what I understand of your testimony yesterday, would it be fair to say that research and development involved the participation of the special-purpose industries?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special-purpose industry only partially participated in research. They didn't have staff for research. There were exceptions. For example, the Crvena Zastava company, which had its own design institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the specific issue of research and development, can you identify for us some of the facilities that were involved in research and development which you have testified were subordinated to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the Military Technical Institute which was the main -- most important institution for research and development, the entire special-purpose industry implemented together with the institute all of the projects that were designed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would kindly ask the witness to either come closer to the the microphone or for his microphones to be adjusted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we help the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I can provide an explanation. The Military Technical Institute did not have any manufacturing facilities. It only had research facilities, and when it comes to the development stage, it was done with the special-purpose industry, namely with those companies that would later on, in the later stages of project development, be involved in the manufacturing of the design product.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the the Military Technical Institute, between the years 1993 and 1995 was the Military Technical Institute one body or a series of bodies subordinated to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the previous state there were three Military Technical Institutes. The first one was of the land army in Belgrade --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, because you said "In the previous state." And when you say "In the previous state" I take it that you are talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let him tell us what he is talking about. What are you talking about when you say "In the previous state"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, where three different institutes existed. The one was of the land army in Belgrade, the Air Force Institute, also in Belgrade, in Zarkovo, to be more precise, and the navy institute, which was located in Zagreb. In 1993 there were still two institutes in existence, the one of the land army and the other of the air force. As for the navy institute, only one department for shipbuilding was established within the Military Technical Institute of the land army. Later on, within the process of transformation in 1994, all the three institutes were merged into one institute whose name was the Military Technical Institute subordinated to the Ministry of Defence. I apologise if --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. After 1995, did the institutes that had been merged into the Military Technical Institute, the one Military Technical Institute subordinated to the Ministry of Defence, did that change, after 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that didn't change. That Military Technical Institute remained as one single institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When I use the term "Military Technical Institute," since yesterday one of the things that was causing some confusion were acronyms, could you please give us the acronym for Military Technical Institute.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The acronym for that institute actually was made up of the first letters of each of the words in the title. So the acronym was VTI.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I want to shift the discussion from the Military Technical Institute with the acronym of VTI subordinated to the Ministry of Defence to the issue and subject matter once again of special-purpose industries. With regard to the production that occurred between 1993 and 1995 of the the special-purpose industries, could you tell us, first of all, whether or not there were special-purpose industries that operated in the Republika Srpska and the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special-purpose industry is actually one complex which leaned on the Federal Ministry Of Defence when it came to the production of weapons and military equipment. Otherwise, those companies were an integral part of the industry of the Republic of Serbia and the industry of the Republic of Montenegro. We dealt with their status together. Those were not military companies. They did not receive allocations from the budget. They were not subordinated to the Ministry of Defence, only when it comes to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kadijevic, clearly you did not understand my question and let me ask you my question again. I'll put it slightly differently and perhaps that will be of further clarification for you. After the break-up of the former Yugoslavia, you have told us that, at least geographically, special-purpose industries existed outside of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Now, my question -- and by "existed," I mean just that they existed, they were physically in other areas. My question is, between the specific years of 1993 and 1995 could you tell us whether or not those special-purpose industries that were physically in Republika Srpska and the Republika Srpska Krajina were operating? And I take it you understand what I mean by the word "operating." Did they produce things or not, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know. All those companies that had existed before the break-up of Yugoslavia and which were found in the territories under the control of different forces, and in this particular case Republika Srpska and Republic of Serbian Krajina, they kept those companies and used them for their own purposes and there were even some civilian companies which received new technologies, new equipment, in order to be able to substitute for those things that could no longer be produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the special-purpose industry in the Republic of Srpska, the Republic of Srpska Krajina and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia between 1993 and 1995, can you tell us whether or not those special purpose industries could autonomously conduct their production and maintenance of technical means or not? Were they autonomous or were they interdependent? If you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that those companies co-operated with the adequate companies in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Before the break-up of Yugoslavia, all those companies belonged to one technological and technical complex. When the country [Realtime transcript read in error "company"] was broken up, most of the companies still depended on co-operation with other companies from the former republics of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm looking at line number 23. It says here "When the company was broken up, most of the the companies still depended ..." Is that the correct language there, "When the the company was broken up," or were you referring to the break-up of the former Yugoslavia, when the country was broken up?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was not talking about the break-up of any companies, I was talking about the break-up of the country. The companies remained existing in that same state and they continued co-operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday when we were discussing the production of the special-purpose industries within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, you told us that there was a diminution of work that was contracted with the special-purpose industry in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. To your knowledge -- and I believe you used the term that sometimes they engage in illegal means. To your knowledge can you tell us, now once again if you know, whether or not the special-purpose industry for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia independently contracted for the production of war materiel outside of the authority of the Ministry of Defence or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in your question there is an ambiguity in terms of the end users of those products. Let me try and answer. When it came to the requirements of the Army of Yugoslavia, companies couldn't and indeed did not clinch deals with the army. They did it with the Ministry of Defence. And if they produced for other end users, they behaved as any other economic subjects, and when it comes to the authority over special-purpose industry, the Ministry of Defence had the control function. It issued permissions. And the production range and annual production plans were all within the hands of the management, so those companies were completely autonomous, completely independent from the Ministry of Defence. Their obligation towards the Ministry of Defence was to keep the same production range and they couldn't change it without the consent of the Ministry of Defence. For example, they could not destroy a production line or sell it and say, this is something we will no longer produce because the Ministry of Defence had invested its own resources into the purchase of all those production lines and technological lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have indicated on line 3, page 9, that their obligation towards the Ministry of Defence was to keep the same production range and they couldn't change it without the consent of the Ministry of Defence. With regard to the production range, first of all, would it be fair to say, or not, that the production capacity of these facilities was greater between 1993 and 1995 than the contract requirements of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, and even during the existence of the SFRY, the production capacities of the entire special-purpose industry surpassed the requirements of the former state of the SFRY and the exports that were envisaged. They had been created as the result of a desire to benefit from the period of favourable production and exports, and the trend was hoped to continue. When the country was broken up, all those capacities became too big because there was no longer export. Bearing that fact in mind, the Ministry of Defence together with the special-purpose industry established the minimum capacities which were needed for the Army of Yugoslavia. The surplus of production capacities, we gave them permission to convert their military purpose production in order to satisfy the needs of civilian production.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the last statement that you've made, the surplus of production capacities, which you say you gave them permission to convert their military purpose production in order to satisfy the needs of civil production, with regard to the issue of the surplus of production capacities, to your knowledge did the special-purpose industries in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia independently contract with either the Republic of Srpska or the Republic of Srpska Krajina with regard to the issue of the production of materiel that would be military purpose production? And by that I mean independent of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such contracts existed back in the SFRY, and as a result of that, these companies continued co-operating among themselves, not only in Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, but also with the Muslim Croat Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's spend a moment on that particular issue, the Muslim Croat Federation. I'm not sure I understand precisely what you mean by that. Could you explain what you mean when you say that these companies continued co-operating with the Muslim Croat Federation.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't specific enough. I meant the companies which were located in the territory within the Muslim Croat Federation. To be more specific, there was a plant in Gorazde which produced certain parts, and then there was the plant producing ammunition in Konjic where companies traded raw materials among themselves without us knowing about that. They simply took a pragmatic, practical approach to solving their problems and contacted each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "without us knowing about it," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the Ministry of Defence first of all, because the Ministry of Defence had the jurisdiction to issue permits for production and for exchange, movement of these goods. It was the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also had indicated that the companies continued to co-operate among themselves, not only in Republika Srpska but Republic of Srpska Krajina. To your knowledge, did the special-purpose industry in FRY privately contract with the Republic of Srpska Ministry of Defence, the VRS, the Republic of Srpska Krajina Ministry of Defence, or the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were contracts with all partners, starting with the Ministry of Defence Main Staffs and the units at a lower level. It was an unregulated system where the procurement and the movement of goods was conducted among various participants.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of movement of goods, yesterday I believe we took a look at an example of certificates that were necessary for goods to be moved from one area to another. I think they were called Certificate Of Passage. What I'm trying to understand here is in order for the movement of goods to occur, for example, let's say between special-purpose industry and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the plant in Gorazde, how would those goods get there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, they did not use legal channels. Directors of these companies would agree upon these transactions among themselves and involve local MUP organs to ensure unhindered passage. They did not seek permits for these activities from the the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've used the acronym here MUP and you've said "local MUP organs." Could you please identify for the Chamber what the acronym "MUP" stands for.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MUP is the acronym for the Ministry of the Interior and their organs, which are located all over the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that what you've just discussed with us would be at best a grey-market and probably black-market activity. What I'd like to -- between the special-purpose industries and the organs that you've identified. I'd like to now discuss, if we could, what the proper procedure and methodology would be for the purpose of obtaining goods through the Ministry of Defence. If you could just explain the methodology and use, let's say, for example, if it's of assistance, the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Srpska making a request. What would the methodology be; how would that work?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The specified procedure when it comes to delivery of military equipment within the FRY was as follows: If Republika Srpska via its own Ministry of Defence approached the Federal Ministry of Defence with a request for armaments and military equipment to be delivered to them, specifying all the details, then, depending on the products that they sought, the Ministry of Defence would approach the companies within the special-purpose industry and inform them about the request for manufacture and delivery. Then these companies would draw up an offer. They would say what they could manufacture, they would quote the price, and the dead-lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could, could we have P511 up on the screen, which would be tab number 5 in your binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, taking a look at this document, if we just take a look at it for a moment and then I'll ask you a question after you've had a chance to look at the entire document.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking a look at this document, and if we can scroll to the second page so that the Chamber is in a position to see the entirety of the document and then we'll go back to the first page because I don't want to dwell terribly long on this document. If the Chamber could note the document is signed by Minister Kovacevic, Republika Srpska Defence Ministry. If we could go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is this generally an example of the kind of procedure that you were just referring to as being the proper procedure that would exist with regard to a request from the Ministry of Defence or from special-purpose industries attempt to engage with some production contract that would include more than one?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is just one element of the transaction and it pertains to the procedure conducted in Republika Srpska. This means that this company here, Pretis Holding, addressed its own Ministry of Defence, that is to say the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, for permission to be issued to them to enter into barter agreement with the Kragujevac Institute for Repairs in order to repair -- to have some of their equipment repaired. And in return, they offered some of the raw materials that could be used in some new manufacturing lines. At the end of this document, you can see that the ministry which issued the permission for this deal was the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, and they say that they would issue a permission for the parity of prices in order to avoid any kind of misuse or abuse, any kind of fraud, when such a barter agreement is concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can take the document off the screen. If we could now have P604 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am sorry, that would be tab 9 in your binder, sir. I apologise. I'd like you to take a look at this document, if you could, please. My question to you: Is this a document that falls within the proper procedure or outside of the proper procedure with regard to the special-purpose industry Pretis?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is evident that this document does not reflect the regular procedure in Republika Srpska. This is their document, coming from Republika Srpska. The director of the Pretis company writes to General Mladic, asking that General Mladic contact General Perisic so that he could intercede on their behalf with the chief of the administration for military economic activities. Normally, the director of this company, Motika, would need to approach Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska and they in turn would need to contact Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and that would be the end of the procedure. If I may add here, General Mladic and General Perisic appear here as, to put it crudely, couriers who were supposed to be a contact for something that is neither within their jurisdiction nor could they deal with it and resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at this document, from this document can we conclude safely that General Perisic - and I'm appreciative of your last answer - that General Perisic has any authority or ability to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the leading nature of this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll rephase.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Does the document as it stands there give us any guidance with regard to the authority that General Perisic may or may not have in terms of the particular request being made by Mr. Motika?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see from the document that General Perisic did not have any competencies and authorities in this matter, no. He was asked to contact the assistant minister for the military economic activity within the Ministry of Defence, and that was below his position and below his responsibilities and competencies. It would have been less of a mistake had this director, Motika, directly contacted this assistant federal minister for military economic activity. That type of communication would have been acceptable, and the only deficiency in that procedure would have been that the two ministers of defence have no knowledge of what the lower organs were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I now would like to take a look at a series of documents that I believe all touch upon the the same transaction. And the first document is P1139. Also included, to make life easier for all, would be P1142, P--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are six documents that all deal with the same transaction, so I'm telling Mr. Registrar the documents that we are going to be dealing with in terms of this entire transaction. P1139 is tab 13 in your binder. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's deal with 1139 first, unless we are able to look at them all at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That, unfortunately, we are not. That is the difficulty with the cyber world, or the electronic world.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at this particular document, what I'd like to, do if we could, is first of all, could you please tell us the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 26th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when was this document received, because I believe there's an indication of it being received in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was received by the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, cabinet of the Chief of Staff on the 3rd of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, before we go any further, is this document concerning a subject matter that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us how you are familiar with the subject matter?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not familiar with the initial document, and based on the correspondence on the first page, you can see that it was not addressed to the Ministry Of Defence. However, in the second document where the ABHO administration, which was in charge of the substance CS, we see that they received from the Federal Ministry of Defence information about what had up until that time the federal ministry done concerning the production and development of this substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that we are going to need to turn to page 3 of the document so that the Chamber is caught up with Mr. Kadijevic in his explanation in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned ABH, I believe this is the document you are referring to. It's page 2, it's here. Now, I'm looking at this document and referring to paragraph number 2. Is that what you are referring to with regard to the Ministry of Defence being involved in the production and development of this substance?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Ministry of Defence, or rather, the administration for research, development, and manufacture had begun this development programme together with the company called Miloje Zakic in Krusevac. At this point in time it was in the final stage, this programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The company that you have mentioned, Miloje Zakic, was that a special-purpose industry or was that another kind of company?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a special-purpose industry company, although part of their facilities manufactured tires and various other rubber products for the civilian sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just for a moment, since you've now mentioned in two separate places the fact that the Ministry of Defence had granted, and where appropriate, a special-purpose industry could deal with civilian production needs, and you mention once again this is a company that is dealing with both military production needs and civilian production needs, in looking at any particular document, can you tell whether or not the facility, the company, is engaged in military production or civilian production if it's not specifically identified? Is there a way of knowing that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not stated explicitly. This here was a large company. Later on they were renamed into Trajal Corporation, and they had several segments and only one segment dealt with the special-purpose production and we invested only in that segment of that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me tell you why I ask you the question, because you mentioned tires and you mentioned that tires were being produced as a civilian production. Now, tires are something which have a universal need, both for the military and for the civilian population, so with regard to those kinds of products that are -- can be equally applied to a civilian use or to a military use, how are we to determine whether or not the production that occurred happened from the civilian part of the plant or from the military part of the plant? Is there a way of determining that by looking at any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this document we cannot establish that because we are not referring to the entire company, Miloje Zakic company, later on Trajal Company. I agree that tires could be produced for the needs of the military but Trajal developed tires autonomously, and if the military needed to purchase tires, then they bought it as regular civilian goods rather than as military equipment. They would conclude regular commercial contracts with them to purchase these tires. The tires were also purchased from a company called Tigar in Pirot. This portion that produced for special-purpose industry was completely separate, and in some instances their facilities were completely separate as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I understand -- would that same situation be true if, for example, the VRS was purchasing tires or the Republika Srpska MOD was interested in purchasing tires? Would they be engaged in the same -- if you know, would they be engaged in the same kind of contractual relationship which you just discussed here, which would be a regular commercial contract?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Irrespective of who the buyer was, those tires were on the market and the Ministry of Defence did not have anything to do that. They couldn't issue permits, they could not ban the sale of those products. Those products were produced from the resources of the company and those tires did not enjoy the status of a military product. Any other product, in order to become part of the military equipment or armament, had to undergo a procedure of testing, and if the testing criteria were met, a decision was issued which stated this particular piece of equipment, nomenclature number and so on and so forth, is hereby adopted as part of the armament and military equipment of the former SFRY and its armed forces and subsequently the Army of Yugoslavia. Without that document, without the preceding prescribed procedure, no equipment could enjoy the status of either military equipment or military armament.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't want to run through an extensive laundry list of items, but take for example one other item, and that would be the production of batteries. Were batteries considered to be an item that would fall within the regular commercial contract that you've discussed, or would batteries fall within some other bailiwick?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krusik, based in Valjevo, had a department called Krusik Batteries and that department produced all sorts of batteries for different purposes, both domestic and foreign. Only a few types of batteries were exclusively for military use for some pieces of equipment of Russian origin and those batteries were developed in order to replace imports. All the other batteries produced by that company were commercial goods on the market and you could purchase those batteries in any specialised shop selling batteries. The Ministry of Defence, when it came to ordering batteries, could order those directly without any special procedure. The batteries produced by that company could be exported without any permits from the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can take this document off the screen. If we could have up on the screen P1142. And that's going to be tab number 14 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the very top of the document there's something that is handwritten. Could you read that, please, for us.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Not without the VSO," which means not with the permission of the Supreme Defence Council. And as for the signature, as far as I'm familiar with the documents that I myself received, I would say that this is the signature of General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking a look at this particular document, could you please explain to us what part of the process is occurring here in terms of the request for the issuance of ammunition, mines, and explosives free of charge.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was preceded by an application of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina which was sent to the Federal Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. You can see from the document that a procedure was being put in place within the jurisdiction of the Federal Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Since the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia did not have at its disposal data about the possibilities and capacities of the Army of Yugoslavia whether there were any surpluses or not, it addressed the office of the Chief of Staff, requesting the Chief of Staff's opinion with this regard. And the General Staff then provides its position, which could be either positive or negative. It informed the Ministry of Defence which thereby prepares a document for the Supreme Defence Council of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this document, two other matters: Could you please tell us what the date is of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was registered with the Federal Ministry of Defence on the 6th of December, 1994. It was registered with the office of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, that document could be taken off the screen. Could we then please have P1143 up on the screen, which is the next tab in your binder, which would be tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, the date of the last document, as you have testified and as indicated on the document, was the 6th. Can you tell us the date of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number -- or the date is 7 December 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And there is a line where it indicates what this is regarding, and could you tell us what it's regarding. By that I mean just what it says there.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As prescribed by the procedure, there is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kadijevic, it says "Re" there. What is it regarding, this language? I just want you to read the language, nothing more for the moment.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regarding your document highly confidential number 1005-3 dated 6 December 1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as you understand this, is this referring to the document that we were just taking a look at? By that I mean P1142.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the previous document, and if you collate the numbers, you can easily see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "collate the numbers," what number are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the number which was registered with the Ministry of Defence, 1005-3, and also the date, 6 December 1994. And the two serve for a complete identification of the two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In this document could you read what it says concerning the position of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of the Chief of Staff of the General Staff is that the final decision should be issued by the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And since in this situation the Chief of the General Staff has deferred the decision-making process to the Supreme Defence Council, what needs to occur? What does this document tell us has to happen? I think, looking at the document, it indicates what the following procedure should be.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the last paragraph it says in that sense it is required that the use of military cabinet of the president of the FRY to the necessary material in order to include the issue on the agenda of the next session of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That document can be taken off the screen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could turn to tab 41 in your binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would be 65 ter 561D. If we could have that document up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your previous testimony you had mentioned the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of the Interior having authority with regard to certain matters. I'd like, if you could, to first of all explain to the Chamber, once again if you know, in general terms the types of authority that the Ministry of the Interior exercised within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia had general competences as any other ministry of any other state, primarily the safety and security of the citizens and their property as well as all the material assets of the state. The ministry maintains order in the territory of the state. That would be the general task of the Ministry of the Interior. Obviously there are also tasks regarding border issues, the movement of hazardous matters, anti-fire protection, and all the other areas where the Ministry of the Interior has a goal to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One of the themes that seems to be prevalent in your testimony is the appropriate procedure that should exist as between a requesting party and a potentially granting party. And I'd like you to take a look at this particular document and tell us if you can, recognising that it's addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, but tell us if you can if the procedure that is set forth herein is, in your estimation based upon your experience, an appropriate procedure?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an appropriate procedure. This is a forced procedure. The initiator of the document, the person who requested certain resources or documents is not familiar with the address to which to write, and when they don't know that, they will most often write to the office of the Chief of Staff and the logic is they will know what to do and they will know who to forward this to. This may be the result of the fact that there is so many re-organisations and transformations and change of competencies. And whenever there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would argue that the witness is speculating in regard to this document. We have no indication that he is familiar with the inner workings of the FRY, VJ, General Staff, nor the Ministry of the Interior, and for him to then go into the mind of who is actually writing these documents I think would be inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let me work with him for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your work in the Ministry of Defence, did you have occasion to have contact with the Ministry of the Interior for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I had direct contacts with the high officials of the Ministry of the Interior. For example, General Obradovic who also testified here in The Hague, he was a member of my own commission for disarmament. Moreover, General Spasic was in charge of anti-fire protection, and together with him I personally dealt with the problem in Milan Blagojevic Lucani company after an incident that resulted in a number of dead and injured. So we dealt with the problem together. We communicated very often because we were the ones to approve the procurement of weapons for the Ministry of the Interior. And they --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go ahead, you may finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they also needed to co-operate with us, hence there was a constantly opened channel of communication. These two ministries, by virtue of their tasks and duties, are forced to engage in very close and constant co-operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you or did you not have experience with and familiarity with the inner workings of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any details, but while I worked at the General Staff I co-operated and I assisted with the equipping of the special brigade of the Ministry of the Interior. I was directly involved in that exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to requests that were made concerning materiel and technical equipment, were you familiar with the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior dealt with such requests when made?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the ministry's work was regulated by regulations both at the federal level and at the republican level. There were documents which described the competencies of each of the ministries and person who was in charge of every -- of all the ministries had to establish an organisation that was also regulated and also discharge duties and tasks within their respective purviews. As far as I know, the procedure and organisation is very similar in all the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to your knowledge and understanding of the General Staff of the VJ, did you have experience in working with the General Staff of the VJ from 1993 and after in your capacity as working within the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that before 1993 I was in the General Staff of the VJ. I was the chief of technical administration, and I was immediately subordinated to the organs of the General Staff. That's why I'm familiar with the technology and procedure of work in the General Staff, both the internal organisation and competencies as well as competencies vis-a-vis other republican federal organs. When I joined the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that co-operation was on a daily basis. I cooperated with General Staff constantly because we co-ordinated in order to draft plans and in order to implement those plans. The same applied to the preparations for the next year's budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Page 25, line 1 you stated -- this is referring to the document that's up on the screen: "This is not an appropriate procedure. This is a forced procedure. The initiator of the document, the person who requested certain resources or documents, is not familiar with the address to which to write, and when they don't know that, they will most often write to the office of the Chief of Staff and the logic is they will know what to do and they will know who to forward this to. This may be the result of the fact that there is so many re-organisations and transformations in change of competencies of the -- and whenever there is --" and you were not in a position to complete your answer because an objection was made. Could you complete your answer at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, again argue that the foundation has not been laid. He has spoken in relation to the federal MUP. We've not discussed at all the entity or his understanding of the Republic of Serbia MUP, and it's still speculation as to the writer himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. It's a bit of a waste of time, but fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Guy-Smith, that is an inappropriate remark to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, yesterday there was a fair amount of confusion with regard to which ministries existed in 1993, and specifically with regard to the issue of the Ministry of Defence with regard to in fact the Republic of Serbia. During your dealings that you have just outlined, did you have occasion before the ministries in the Republic of Serbia were integrated into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, as you testified to yesterday, did you have opportunity to have contact and experiences with individuals in the Ministry of the Interior for the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just gave you the names of two generals, Obradovic and Spasic. They were not from the Federal Ministry of the Interior but from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And when we had this accident in Lucani, the minister of the interior of Serbia was engaged in the investigation and finalising the procedure. And the director, although a colonel in the Yugoslavia army, was arrested as a result of that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were you, as you've answered with regard to the Ministry of the Interior for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, were you aware of the procedures and workings that were utilized by the Ministry of the Interior for Republic of Serbia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Ministry of the Interior had no special competencies because the republics had taken over those competencies. They were mostly focused on protecting foreign diplomatic premises in Belgrade, and in the beginning they had one brigade of the federal MUP. It was the republics who carried the bulk of the work and they had a completely independent system of the Internal Affairs, both Montenegro and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the Ministry of the Interior for the Republic of Serbia, were you familiar with their inner workings in your experience?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the extent to which I had contact with them. I co-operated with them on the tasks that we carried out jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I just want to clear something here which I don't understand. I think I might as well go to a page I can control. Mr. Kadijevic, at page 29, line 7, let's go to line 8, you were asked: "Were you aware of the procedures and workings that were utilized by the Ministry of the Interior for the Republic of Serbia in 1993?" Your answer was: "The Federal Ministry of the Interior had no special competences because the republics had taken over those competences." Now, in 1993, which republics are you referring to in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Republic of Serbia there was just one republic, the Republic of Serbia, and the other member of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was the Republic of Montenegro. So FRY consisted of two republics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, you confuse me. You are taking me back to yesterday's problem. We are talking here about the Republic of Serbia, now you are introducing the word "FRY." I'm not quite sure, when the parties talk about the Republic of Serbia, what they are talking about. Can you just tell me what you are talking about, because I really don't follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yesterday I tried to exclude from the SFRY all the republics that had left, which left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hold it there. We are talking here in 1993. What was the Republic of Serbia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In accordance with the constitution, the Republic of Serbia in 1993 had two autonomous provinces, Vojvodina, Kosovo, and it had the central Serbia. Those parts comprised the Republic of Serbia according to the constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are you saying then that the Federal Ministry of the Interior had no competences because all those competences had been taken by those three republics, by the two republics and that Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vojvodina remained within the composition of the Republic of Serbia. As for the federal ministry, the only competency it kept was the security they provided to the diplomatic offices in Belgrade, and they had forces to provide that. All other competencies of the Federal Ministry of the Interior were taken over by the member republics, republics members of the Federation, and those were Serbia and Montenegro. The Federal Ministry of the Interior remained in place only to co-ordinate the work between the two republican ministries of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you know, who did the MUP of Serbia buy NVO from? First of all, do you know what I mean when I say "NVO"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "NVO" stands for armaments and military equipment. I have already explained that something could be termed to be NVO only if previously they -- those goods were put on the list of armaments and military equipment of the Army of Yugoslavia. The ministry used some of the equipment that came from that list and they also had some other additional equipment that did not exist within the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "ministry," because we've been dealing with a number of different ministries, which seems to be causing some level of confusion, the term that you just used there "ministry" refers to which ministry? When you said, "The ministry used some of the equipment that came from that list," what ministry are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia used some of the equipment that came from that list, where did they go to to get that equipment? Who did they request that equipment from?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the procedure, they were supposed to request this from the Federal Ministry of Defence, which is what they did; however, there were cases when they would conclude contracts directly with companies from the special-purpose industry using the same procedure used by the Army of Yugoslavia. That is to say, they would sign contracts with them and purchase these products with their own money.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is understood. With regard to the document that is up on the screen, the second paragraph states: "Since their request does not come under the authority of the Yugoslav Army General Staff, we are asking for your opinion, if you are unable to grant the request within your authority." Can you tell us, looking at this document - if you can that's fine, and if you can't that's fine - why the position would be taken by the Yugoslav Army General Staff that this request does not come under its authority?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska from Bijeljina should not communicate directly with the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. There's no procedure that provides for that. The Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska was supposed to send its request to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. That was the proper channel that the ministries -- identical ministries deal with each other. That is to say Ministry of the Interior deals with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Is -- if you know, is that why this states that their request does not come under the authority of the Yugoslav Army General Staff because, as you just said, a Ministry of the Interior has to deal with the Ministry of the Interior and not to deal with the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. In this particular case, the General Staff could have acted differently. They could have sent back to the sender this document, this letter. That would not have been professional and that would not have been fair, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the language at the end of the sentence dealing with granting their request within your authority, can you expand at all on what the meaning of that particular language is in regards to this document? If you can, that's fine, and if you can't, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the final portion of the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This portion means this: If the republic Ministry of the Interior is unable to grant this request, then they were supposed to inform the office of the Chief of the General Staff so that they could respond to the person initiating this request and close the circle thus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would move the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D452. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go to tab number 44.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could go to tab number 44 in your binder, which would be 65 ter 704D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at this document, and after you've had an opportunity to look at the document, I believe the document is a number of pages long. It's three pages in English, it may be only two in B/C/S. After you've had a chance to take a look at this document, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because I held it in my hands. This is the plan for implementation of the conclusion of the 21st session of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this plan, were you or were you not present at the 21st session of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not attend a single session of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this plan being predicated on the conclusions of the 21st session of the Supreme Defence Council, how did you become aware of what those conclusions were?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the conclusions of the Supreme Defence Council, the Ministry of Defence as a competent organ vis-a-vis certain conclusions received this document. The office of the minister of defence drew up a document based on this and sent it to various organs within the Ministry of Defence indicating who is supposed to carry out which task and within what time-limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us what the date of this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is dated 29th of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could turn to the next page, please, which is entitled "Plan," which is the plan itself. And taking a look at item number 3, which indicates some involvement with the Russian Federation, could you explain to us what was occurring with regard to item number 3.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3 reads: "Assess possibilities for importing weapons, military equipment, and spare parts from the Russian Federation, charging it to the current balance, and propose a way to perform the task."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to item number 4, could you explain to us what is the plan with regard to item number 4.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 4 reads: "Pursuant to the proposal of the Federal Ministry of Defence on co-operation with the People's Republic of China, the Supreme Defence Council decided to accept the proposal of the Federal Ministry of Defence with the requirement that the interests of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia be protected with an adequate contract concept. The contract should oblige the People's Republic of China not to provide information on the MPG 1200 horsepower to Pakistan."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you explain to the Chamber, if you know, why the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was concerned about being protected with regard to a contract that was being entered into with the People's Republic of China as it related to Pakistan?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Ministry of Defence developed the motor and fuel group of 1200 horsepower, which was an improvement on the Russian model which had 1000 horsepower and it was used for tank 72 and M-84 tank. When a number of countries learned of this technical improvement of the tank motor which enabled it to have a much better performance, there was suddenly a great surge in demand for this motor of 1200 horsepower. We had a request from the Federal Republic of China and from Pakistan. The Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued us permission to co-operate with the Federal Republic of China, whereas there were certain conditions in relation to co-operation with regard to Pakistan. And we were not given subsequently green light to continue negotiations. By way of this conclusion, the Supreme Defence Council allowed us to engage in negotiations with the People's Republic of China concerning the motor of 1200 horsepower.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking a look at the next paragraph, I'd like to focus your attention on the following sentence, which is the second sentence in that paragraph, that says: "No direct agreements and deliveries of NVO can be made and special-purposes industrial enterprises cannot deliver or sell NVO to anyone without the approval of the SMO with the exception of planned deliveries for the VJ." Now, you previously, I believe, defined each of these acronyms, so there should be no confusion. I'd like for you to explain the very last clause in that sentence which is, "with the exception of planned deliveries for the VJ."

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This formulation is perhaps a clumsy one. This is how it was drawn up in the office of the federal minister for defence because it says in addition to planned deliveries for the Army of Yugoslavia where we do not issue separate permit because we had negotiated this ourselves, we, the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. In looking through this document, there's another acronym here that exists in all but one of them which is, under the responsible party, it says SVPD of the SMO. Could you please define that acronym for us.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an acronym for the sector for military economic activity of the Federal Ministry of Defence. The Ministry of Defence had a number of sectors, this is how it was organised, so this was the sector for military economic activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And for purposes of completion of understanding, there is another acronym in this document, and that's in paragraph number 2 and that's UFiB of the SMO. Could you please tell us what that acronym stands for.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an acronym for administration for finance and budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I would move its admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D453. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like you to now go to tab 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 814D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, when it comes up, the document is entitled, at least in English, "Session Agreement." And I'd like to know whether or not you are familiar with these types of documents.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber what a session agreement is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an agreement whereby a contractual party transfers a debt on to another third party with which it negotiates a new deal.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I am sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would appreciate the assistance of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, I have nothing on my screen and I'm struggling to find the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what I was just about to comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Welcome to the club.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was just about to say that I would appreciate the assistance of the technical staff in making black screens have some kind of image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's been reported to the technical staff and I can tell you I'm also in the same boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You beat me to the punch, Mr. Thomas. I am a bit hard-pressed to continue. I'm going to be dealing with a number of -- directly dealing with documents for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To what extent does that inconvenience you, Mr. Thomas and Madam Carter? I have no way of knowing what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm also informed that Mr. Perisic is without screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think he is the most important person here. Mr. Lukic -- Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm sorry, with the hard copies are you not in a position to carry on?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I still have the same problem for Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document also be provided to the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam court usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does everybody who has to see the document now have it before them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I assume that if you do, all the other booths have, and a nod will help me from this booth. You do have it? Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were explaining what this type of a document was and you indicated on page 38 at line 10: "This is an agreement whereby a contractual party transfers a debt on to another third party with which it negotiates a new deal." Now, looking at paragraph 1, there is a name there, could you read it and tell us if you recognise that particular name.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that's item number 2. Item number 1?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 1 is the [indiscernible] production in Uzice and the abbreviation at the beginning stands for the First Partisan and that was the name of that particular factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at this particular document, are you familiar with this particular transaction?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not familiar with this particular transaction because it involved the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska and the First Partisan company in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your experience in the Ministry of Defence for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did you engage in like contracts with other special-purpose industries?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Ministry of Defence, or rather, its administration for procurement, which was in charge of all contracts, also negotiated session deals with various suppliers and producers. This is an aspect of business which is put in place in order to make payments or receive payments for the services provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would move the admission of this document for the limited purpose of an example of a session agreement since the witness has indicated that he has no familiarity with this specific transaction, but is familiar with the document and the purpose of these types of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: As an exemplar, I have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that document shall be assigned Exhibit D454. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Tab number 48, good sir, which will be 65 ter 983D. I'd like you to take a look at this document and then I'll discuss it with you. Could you first of all tell us the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 29 July 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the author of this document is who, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author of this document is at the office of the Ministry of Defence, in its final version, and the document was, drafted or rather, prepared by the sector for military economic activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to take a look at the second full paragraph, which I believe starts off with the language, "Regardless of how the situation develops ..." Could you read -- could you read the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Irrespective of the developments, the federal government has to redistribute resources in the federal and republican budgets in order to provide an additional 35.300.000 dinars to finance the adopted measures and procure materiel and technical equipment necessary to raise the combat readiness of the Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And were you at all involved in this particular concern, which is the need to redistribute funds for the procurement of materiel and technical equipment to raise the combat readiness of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector for military economic activities, together with administration for finances and budget, we were aware of the surpluses of the special-purpose industry and we arrived at the amount of 35.300.000 dinars which corresponded to the request of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia for the procurement of the most necessary means in order to raise the combat readiness of the army. Those are not normal requirements. Those requirements were meant to meet just the minimum needs of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could now turn to the next sentence, which I believe starts with the language, "Engaging these funds ..." could you please read that.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Federal Ministry for Defence will engage these and the financial resources provided by the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, to service their needs, will organise the production and procurement of materiel and technical equipment."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would ask this document be marked for identification, and the reason for that is that two places in the English there's the word "earmark." The first time Mr. Kadijevic said that the federal government must "redistribute" an amount, and the second time he used the word "provided." And earmarking and providing and earmarking and redistributing are vastly different concepts, so I think if we could have this marked for identification, because this document needs to be double-checked with regard to the issue of translation. Other than that, I move its admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No objection to the MFI status, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D455 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Tab number 49, please, which would be 65 ter 984D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to take a look at this document, Mr. Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've had an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell us the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 5 August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this document, as I understand it, was signed by a gentleman by the name Sava Pustinja. Do you know that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time Lieutenant-General Sava Pustinja was the chief of sector for military economics activity and on this particular occasion he was acting on behalf of the federal minister of defence, who was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you please read for us the very first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Please find enclosed a decision by the federal government on a cessation of political and economic relations with Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm a bit confused. The document that we just were looking at that's been marked for identification is dated the 29th of July 1994. And it seems what this document is in fact talking about economic relations with the Republika Srpska, and here, about a week later, there seems to be an about face on this issue. Do you have any knowledge about what happened here? Can you help us out at all in terms of what happened with regard to this document dated the 5th of August, 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Carter. Sorry, Mr. Kadijevic. Yes, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the end of the question is certainly not leading, I would argue that having Defence counsel compare and contrast two separate documents and then ask the witness to do the same thing is an inappropriate use. It's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I fail to understand the objection in the manner that it's been put because I think that Ms. Carter misapprehends the question itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, am I wrong to say that the previous document was a session between Republika Srpska and a company in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, the last document we discussed was the document that we MFI'd because there were two issues concerning the word "earmarked." That was the last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's a document between the Federal Ministry of Defence -- it's a document about the Federal Ministry of Defence for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. It has nothing to do with Republika Srpska with regard to any interactions as between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what did it deal with, I'm sorry, I still don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It dealt with redistributing 35.300.000 dinars to finance adoptive measure and engaging these funds and funds provided by the Republika Srpska for their own needs, that the Federal Ministry of Defence will organise the production and procurement of materiel and technical equipment. So this is a document, this was a ministry -- Federal Ministry of Defence of the FRY internal document, discussing what they are going to be proceeding to do. The next document is a Federal Ministry of Defence document in which there's an indication that there's going to be a cessation of political and economic relations with Republika Srpska and my question is can you be of any help here?
